exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Planning a Museum Visit
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Hi Jack! Are you free this Saturday? There's a new art exhibition at the city museum.
Jack: That sounds great, Mia. What kind of art is it?
Mia: It's all about abstract painting. My art teacher says it's amazing.
Jack: I've never really understood abstract art. Will we be able to understand it?
Mia: Don't worry. There's a free guide who explains the ideas behind each painting.
Jack: Perfect. What time should we meet?
Mia: Let's meet at the museum gate at ten in the morning.
Jack: Ten o'clock is fine. I'm really excited now. See you on Saturday!
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 邀 Jack 周六去市博物馆看新展;是抽象画展,老师说很棒;Jack 担心看不懂抽象艺术;Mia 说有免费讲解员解释每幅画背后的想法;两人约定周六上午十点在博物馆门口见。

options: He may not understand abstract art.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Where Artists Find Ideas
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Where do artists get their ideas? The answer is different for everyone.
For some, childhood memories are the richest source of inspiration.
Others find new ideas while travelling to faraway places.
Many artists say that nature, with its colours and shapes, never stops inspiring them.
In the end, inspiration can come from anywhere, as long as we keep our eyes and hearts open.
exercises.translation_cn: 艺术家从哪里获得创意?答案因人而异;对一些人来说,童年记忆是最丰富的灵感来源;另一些人在远方旅行中找到新点子;许多艺术家说大自然的色彩与形状永远启发着他们;只要保持眼睛和心灵的开放,灵感可来自任何地方。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

What never stops inspiring many artists?
options: Nature, with its colours and shapes.

questions.stem: According to the passage, where can inspiration come from?
options: Almost anywhere, if we stay open.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Talking about a Sculpture
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Tom: Lily, did you see that huge sculpture in the city square?
Lily: Yes! The one made of metal wire and lights? It was breathtaking.
Tom: I agree. At night it looked like a giant fish floating in the air.
Lily: I heard the artist got the idea from an old folk tale.
Tom: Really? Which tale?
Lily: The story of a fish jumping through the Dragon Gate.
Tom: That's clever. I was amazed that cold metal could feel so alive.
Lily: Me too. I think it's the most creative work I've seen this year.
exercises.translation_cn: Tom 问 Lily 是否看过城市广场那座巨大雕塑;是金属丝和灯做的,很震撼;夜里像漂浮在空中的大鱼;Lily 听说灵感来自一个古老的民间故事——鱼跃龙门;Tom 惊讶冰冷的金属竟能如此有生命;两人都认为这是今年看过最有创意的作品。

questions.stem: What was the sculpture made of?

options: A giant fish floating in the air.

questions.stem: Where did the artist get the idea?

options: A fish jumping through the Dragon Gate.

questions.stem: How did Tom feel about the sculpture?
options: Amazed that metal could feel so alive.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Art and Technology
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Technology is changing the way we enjoy art.
In the past, people had to travel far to see a famous painting.
Today, a digital version can be shown on a giant screen for everyone.
With 3D animation, the figures in an old painting seem to move and breathe.
In this way, great art has become more accessible to ordinary people than ever before.
exercises.translation_cn: 科技正在改变我们欣赏艺术的方式;过去人们要远行才能看到一幅名画;如今数字版可以在巨幕上向所有人展示;借助3D动画,古画中的人物仿佛会动、会呼吸;这样,伟大的艺术比以往任何时候都更贴近普通人。

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Choosing an Artwork to Write About
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Teacher: For today's writing task, choose one artwork that makes a strong impression on you.
Sara: Mr Lee, can I write about the Floating Fish sculpture?
Teacher: Of course, Sara. Why did you choose it?
Sara: Because it shows how an old folk tale can inspire something modern.
Teacher: That's a wonderful reason. Remember to describe how it makes you feel.
Sara: I felt amazed and a little moved when I saw it.
Teacher: Good. Use words like 'inspiring' and 'breathtaking' to express your feelings.
Sara: Thank you, Mr Lee. I can't wait to start writing.
exercises.translation_cn: 老师布置写作任务:选一件给你深刻印象的艺术品;Sara 问能否写《漂浮的鱼》雕塑;老师问她为何选它;Sara 说它展现了古老民间故事如何启发现代作品;老师提醒她要写出自己的感受;Sara 说看到时既惊叹又有些感动;老师建议用 inspiring、breathtaking 这样的词表达感受;Sara 迫不及待要动笔。

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 A Tip for Finding Inspiration
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple tip for anyone who wants to find their own inspiration.
First, slow down and look carefully at the small things around you.
A leaf, a shadow or an old photo can all start a great idea.
Second, keep a notebook and write down anything that interests you.
Inspiration rarely arrives all at once; it grows from the details we notice every day.
exercises.translation_cn: 给任何想找到自己灵感的人一个简单的小贴士:第一,慢下来,仔细观察身边的小事物;一片叶子、一道影子或一张旧照片都能引出一个好点子;第二,随身带个本子,把任何让你感兴趣的东西记下来;灵感很少一下子到来,它从我们每天留意的细节中生长出来。
